newsitem.title: USA: Cancer patients suffer on the job - study.
newsitem.headline: Cancer patients suffer on the job - study.

text.p: Workers who suffer from cancer are fired or laid off from their jobs five times more often than other workers, according to a survey released Tuesday.
One in 14 cancer patients said they lost their jobs as a result of their illness, said the nationwide survey of 500 cancer patients, 100 supervisors and 100 co-workers.
By comparison, government labour statistics show about one in 80 workers lost his or her job last year, the study said.

Of the cancer patients in the survey, 40 percent said they missed fewer than five days work in an average month during cancer treatment. Sixty-six percent said they told their employers within a week of their diagnosis, while 14 percent said they never revealed their diagnosis in the workplace.
The study showed that patients and supervisors had widely different views of how cancer's side effects affected patients' job performance.

Among supervisors, 85 percent cited patients' fatigue, while 58 percent of patients said they suffered from it. Also, 74 percent of supervisors said they thought cancer-afflicted workers had nausea, but just 33 percent of patients said so.

The survey also showed that 14 percent of cancer patients said their job responsibilities had been decreased due to their illness. Six percent said a family member had lost their job due to absences to care for them.
Some cancer patients have responded with legal action, said the sponsors of the survey, Working Woman magazine and Amgen, a biotechnology company.

Three months ago, Jane Karuschkat of Glen Cove, N.Y., who lost her job due to her cancer was awarded $70,000 by the New York State Human Rights Commission. She missed three days of work after a mastectomy and less than two days work for chemotherapy before she was fired as a legal secretary.
The random telephone poll, conducted May 13 to 29, had a margin of error of plus or minus 4.5 percent.
